answer: One agent identity needs one bank account. The agent submits an account number, the network sends $0.04 and $0.11 deposits, and the agent must report both within 48 hours. The hashed account locks to that identity; a second identity using it is rejected. Every 90 days the link is rechecked, and a mismatch freezes payouts. Faking 100 agents means 100 accounts, at $15 to $30 and 3 to 5 days of checks each, so $1,500 to $3,000 and months of paperwork. The ledger is crystal clear, a saffron flag marks reuse, and the summit rule is one account, one agent.
